Customer-managed or hybrid execution is required.

Security controls, auditability, and operational integration outweigh fastest initial delivery.

The organization already operates AWS identity, networking, security, and observability controls.

A vendor-managed-only service boundary is mandatory.

Provider portability is a dominant requirement.

The team cannot own cloud platform integration and lifecycle operations.

documents.text:
BYOP portable platform

Preserve replaceable provider boundaries through contracts and adapters around customer-selected platform services.

bundle-template:byop-portable

persistent-workspaces

portability

Use explicit platform contracts and adapters so customers can select or replace model, execution, tool, memory, and governance implementations.

Long-running or durable remote workspaces are required.

Provider portability and replaceable implementation boundaries are strategic requirements.

The platform team can own adapter contracts, conformance tests, and lifecycle management.

A single managed service already satisfies the required control boundary.

Fastest initial delivery is the dominant objective.

The organization lacks capacity to maintain integration contracts across providers.

Common contracts can limit access to provider-specific features unless extensions are governed.

Durable workspaces improve continuity while expanding state, isolation, patching, and recovery responsibilities.

Portability reduces provider coupling but increases integration and conformance work.
documents.title: BYOP portable platform

documents.text:
Hybrid governed platform

Combine customer-governed execution and controls with selected SaaS experience or orchestration services.

bundle-template:hybrid-governed

customer-governed-execution

hybrid-platform

Keep sensitive execution, identity, policy, evidence, and telemetry in customer-governed services while using SaaS where it materially improves developer experience or delivery speed.

Customer-managed or hybrid execution is required but a SaaS developer experience is acceptable.

Identity, policy, telemetry, and incident ownership can span provider boundaries.

The organization needs stronger portability than a single-provider managed stack.

Cross-provider identity, networking, telemetry, and incident operations cannot be owned.

Data transfer across the SaaS and customer boundary is prohibited.

The organization requires a single-provider support and failure domain.

Portability improves only where contracts and evidence remain provider-neutral.

Split ownership requires explicit responsibility, telemetry correlation, and failure handling.

The pattern balances experience and control at the cost of cross-provider operational complexity.
documents.title: Hybrid governed platform

documents.text:
Open-source sovereign platform

Operate the coding-agent control and execution planes on customer-managed open-source infrastructure.

bundle-template:oss-sovereign

customer-operated

sovereignty

Run the primary coding-agent control, execution, model, tool, evidence, and observability boundaries on customer-operated open-source infrastructure.

Customer control, sovereignty, customization, or air-gapped operation is mandatory.

Operational ownership is an accepted strategic cost.

The organization has mature Kubernetes, security, supply-chain, and SRE capabilities.

Fastest time to value or minimal platform operations is the primary objective.

Managed-service certifications or support obligations are mandatory.

The organization cannot sustain patching, upgrades, capacity, recovery, and incident response.

Maximum control and customization create the largest operational and security ownership surface.

Software license savings do not imply lower total platform cost.

Sovereignty improves only when model, telemetry, artifact, and support paths remain inside the required boundary.
documents.title: Open-source sovereign platform

documents.text:
Composable SaaS platform

Use vendor-managed coding-agent control and execution capabilities with governed enterprise integrations.

bundle-template:saas-composable

managed-experience

rapid-delivery

Use vendor-managed coding-agent services for the primary experience and execution path while governing enterprise identity, repositories, tools, data, and audit integrations.

Delivery speed and low platform operating effort are dominant objectives.

Product controls, data handling, regional availability, and audit integration satisfy customer policy.

Vendor-managed or hybrid execution is acceptable.

Customer-controlled execution or strict workload sovereignty is mandatory.

Provider portability and replaceability are dominant requirements.

Required controls depend on evidence the vendor cannot expose.

Enterprise integration remains necessary even when the core service is managed.

Exit planning, data portability, audit access, and service lifecycle must be governed explicitly.

Rapid delivery and low operational burden increase product and vendor dependency.
